data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 proposes a 'temporal-spatial signature' / 'latent synchronization' test, but its own counterconditions refute its sufficiency as evidence that would distinguish hidden-correlation from independence. When a shared cause triggers failures at widely varying intervals, the temporal signature is masked; when heterogeneity makes the shared cause produce completely different symptoms, the dependency-graph signature is obscured. These are common in real decentralized networks (independent operators have different update cadences, load, and configs), so the target's distinguishing evidence fails in exactly the high-variance regime the question targets.
